Definition: a robe (i.e. upper and outer garment)
BiblicalUsage: A robe is the outer garment, and the Bible uses it for priests, for kings, and for righteousness itself: the robe of the ephod is made of blue with bells of gold, Hannah makes Samuel a little coat every year, and Saul catches Samuel's skirt and tears it. Tamar wears a garment of divers colours, and Job says he put on righteousness and it clothed him like a robe.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the robe is the picture of being clothed by another: Samuel's mother made his coat, the priest's robe was God's design, and Job's righteousness was a garment he put on. The best robe in the Bible is the one God gives, and it fits because He made it.
RelatedPeople: Aaron; Samuel; Hannah; King Saul; Job
